newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Rio state confident of selling Banerj today.
newsitem.headline: Rio state confident of selling Banerj today.

text.p: Rio de Janeiro state is confident that the privatization auction of its bank Banerj will take place as planned at 1600 local time/1500 EDT/1900 GMT today, a spokeswoman for the Rio state Finance office said.
She said only legal challenges could prevent the bank from being auctioned, adding that so far there are no court injunctions suspending the sale.

In a preemptive measure, Brazil's Central Bank extended its special administration of Banerj, which expires today, for 15 days, giving the state more time to sell the bank if the sale has to be postponed again for any reason.
Although everything appears to be ready for the sale, a local newspaper said Banerj could not be privatized because of a lack of investor interest.

Citing unnamed bank sources, O Estado de Sao Paulo daily Thursday said Bradesco and Banco Itau, two of the four preidentified bidders, would not bid because they are not satisfied by the guarantees Rio is giving to cover Banerj's pension and payroll-related debts.
Both banks have declined to say they would bid, restricting themselves to saying that they are analysing the deal.

Banerj's pension and payroll-related debts will be assumed by Rio state and covered by a 3.088 billion real loan from federal mortgage bank Caixa Economica Federal (CEF). The loan was approved by the Senate late Tuesday.
After several postponements, the Banerj sale, which had been scheduled for Wednesday, was delayed until today because administrative details regarding the loan had to be settled.
Rio state will sell Banerj, the first Brazilian state-owned bank due to be privatized, for at least 310 million reais in a closed-envelope auction on the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.
